newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state commission recommends utility merger.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state commission recommends utility merger.

text.p: The staff of the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission (WUTC) on Monday recommended approval of a proposed merger between Puget Sound Power and Light Co. and Washington Energy Co., the parent of Washington Natural Gas Co.
A final decision by the three-member commission is expected early next year.
The staff said electric and natural gas customers in western Washington should see a slight reduction in their rates as a result of the merger.
The companies had proposed no increases in natural gas rates from 1997 through 2001 and an electric rate hike of 1 percent a year for the first four years with no changes in 2001.
The WUTC staff said the pending merger, by creating a single provider of electricity and natural gas service, would lead to savings of $166 million over a five-year period.
Concerns were expressed, however, of a possible deterioration in service and the staff recommended that a comprehensive service quality program be instituted.
The staff recommendation is one of 19 parties submitting testimony on the merger to the state commission.
The two utilities announced plans to merge in October 1995 and formally filed an application with the Washington commission in February.
